assertion.statement: For the actual finite CM raising diagram at a permitted inert prime ell, a common finite local extension supplies good models and the cyclic prime-to-ell N-level subgroups; every degree-ell raising isogeny reduces to relative ell-Frobenius followed by an isomorphism, with its kernel and level image specializing accordingly.
assertion.objects: One finite diagram of actual CM raising isogenies and cyclic N-level subgroups at a permitted inert new prime ell.
assertion.hypotheses: Actual finite generic CM diagram over number fields, degree-ell raising isogenies with duals, cyclic N-level subgroups, ell outside6dND_K, and the separately supplied inert CM supersingularity criterion. CM integrality and potential-good reduction are applied explicitly to construct the good models.
assertion.quantifiers: Every isogeny in that fixed finite diagram and its chosen specialization.
assertion.parameter_range: ell outside6dND_K; no prime-toell restriction on the isogeny degree.
assertion.uniformity: One finite extension may depend on the finite diagram; no single extension for all conductors.
assertion.constants: Rank and special degree remain exactly ell.
assertion.normalizations: Relative ell-power Frobenius, then an isomorphism of elliptic curves with the transported level subgroup.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Does not construct the generic CM diagram or prove its supersingularity criterion; the fixed modular parametrization extends by the separate integral-map input. No uniform local extension over all conductors is claimed.
assertion.limit_order: Fix finite generic diagram; apply integral-j potential-good reduction and isogeny invariance; extend maps and duals; prove finite flat rank and extend prime-to-ell level; then identify Frobenius specialization.

use.reason: Supplies the degree-preserving specialization missing from the supersingularity and integral-parametrization inputs; prime-toell etaleness is not used.
use.shared_contract_justification: Main3842–3846 and the supporting note33–37 use the same raising-kernel and level-subgroup specialization.
